subdivision","b":"Sculpt a single mesh of more than 500 million polygons on one 16 GB graphics card. Every brush, alpha and mask works at that density, with fast undo, and sculpt layers work too.","w":["Outliner \u203a poly object \u203a Level + \u203a Auto \u00b7 Tiles \u00b7 Normal","Settings \u203a Preferences \u203a Poly \u203a Subdivide as tiles from"]},{"g":"n","t":"Alpha Studio: paint your own brush alphas","b":"Paint the black-and-white alpha of a stamp brush directly in Klay. Every edit applies to the brush as you paint. The Stamp button of the bottom toolbar opens a small studio above it, with the alpha's name, undo, a gray or clay preview and your favourite stamps; Studio opens the full one.","w":["Brush panel \u203a Alpha stamp \u203a Studio"]},{"g":"n","t":"Dynamic alpha brushes: a different stamp for each pressure","b":"A stamp brush can now change its alpha with pen pressure: a light touch lays one shape, a firm press another, and the stamp blends between them along the stroke. Paint the shapes in Alpha Studio, each on its own layer, and give a layer a range of pressure with its pressure button (Min, Max and Softness).","w":["Brush panel \u203a Alpha stamp \u203a Studio \u203a layer pressure button"]},{"g":"n","t":"ZBrush .ztl import (alpha)","b":"Klay now opens ZBrush tool files (.ztl) from Import model, the file browser or a drag and drop. Each subtool arrives at its highest subdivision level with its UVs and polypaint, and its lower levels are rebuilt to match ZBrush's subdivision count. Files saved below the top level and files from ZBrush 2021 are supported.","w":["Import model \u203a .ztl"]},{"g":"n","t":"Record a sculpt as an OBJ sequence","b":"New recording opens a setup card. A recording can go to a Klay cache, as before, or to a sequence of OBJ files, one per snapshot, reduced to a polygon limit such as 1M or 200k with the Decimation tool's settings. The reduction runs in the background, and every file is one closed mesh.","w":["Timeline \u203a Record \u203a New recording"]},{"g":"n","t":"A camera that follows a Klay motion recording","b":"A camera can film a loaded recording on its own: it orbits outside the sculpture and turns to look where the sculpture is changing, on smooth springs. Smoothness, Bounce, Orbit speed and Idle drift set how it moves; Muffle and Memory decide whether a single stroke elsewhere draws it away or only sustained work does; Face the change, Close-up, Distance and Height set the framing; the camera can come close to the surface without entering the sculpture.","w":["Camera card \u203a Follow Klay motion","Outliner \u203a recording \u203a Speed \u00b7 Interpolation \u00b7 Camera"]},{"g":"n","t":"Modifier tab: fields and copies without extra objects","b":"The Modifier tab replaces the Field tab in a poly object's outliner card. Fields are now one of its modifiers: the Soft field card, with + Field and From mask inside it. The tab also holds copy modifiers that draw copies of the object without adding rows to the outliner: Mirror, Radial, Array, Grid, Spiral and Phyllotaxis. Mirror reflects across the world axes by default, or across the object's own pivot and axes with Space set to Object. Radial turns its copies around the object, the world origin or the transform gizmo's centre, set by Centre. The copies draw instanced with level of detail, so a stack can make up to 32,768 of them, such as a 20 \u00d7 20 \u00d7 20 grid. They stack in order, so a Mirror above a Radial doubles every copy, and every copy modifier except Mirror can randomize the scale, rotation and position of each copy.","w":["Outliner \u203a poly object \u203a Modifier \u203a + Modifier"]},{"g":"n","t":"Flood processes on clay layers","b":"With a clay layer selected, the Flood tab lists six processes for the whole layer: Round edges, Chamfer edges, Inflate clay, Shell, Noise displace and Remove floating bits. Round and Chamfer act on every edge sharper than a chosen angle, which suits hard-surface models converted to clay. The layer updates while the sliders move, and Apply keeps the result as one undo step.","w":["Flood tab \u203a Add \u203a Clay"]},{"g":"n","t":"Straight clay strokes with Shift","b":"Pressing Shift during an Add, Carve or Stamp stroke on a clay layer turns the stroke into a straight line from where it started to the cursor. A preview line follows the mouse, and on release the clay is laid as one straight line and one undo step, ending on the surface under the cursor. A spaced stamp brush keeps its spacing along the line. Escape or a right click cancels the line.","w":["Clay tab \u203a Add \u00b7 Carve \u00b7 Stamp \u203a stroke + Shift"]},{"g":"n","t":"Normals: smooth, hard or by angle","b":"The Normals dialog sets how a poly object shades: Smooth makes every edge soft, Hard makes every face flat, and By angle makes edges sharper than the chosen angle hard, 30\u00b0 by default, as the import does. Hard is a display setting and does not change the mesh. By angle adds vertices only along the hard edges, so sculpting is unaffected and an organic mesh is left as it is. Each Apply is one undo step, and saved scenes keep the result.","w":["Outliner \u203a poly object \u203a Normals\u2026","Functions \u203a Process \u203a Normals"]},{"g":"n","t":"Point handles on curve dots","b":"Every dot of the selected curve has a small handle beside it. Hovering or clicking the handle opens the dot's actions in a ring around it: Bezier, Linear corner, Twist, Scale, Bevel, IK, Lock and Delete. Click an action to toggle it, or press the handle and release over an action in one movement. Twist, Scale and Bevel are dials: press and turn around the dot, or pull away from it; a double-click resets them.","w":["Curve tool \u203a dot \u203a handle"]},{"g":"n","t":"Planar stamps and clay brushes","b":"A new Planar option fits a plane to the surface around the cursor as you stroke and keeps the brush from rising above it, so a stamp no longer jumps onto a raised plateau. Plane offset moves the plane up or down, Area radius sets how wide an area of surface it is fitted to, and Modifier inverts planar lets the invert key flip the offset. The DISKO stamp has it on.","w":["Brush \u203a Placement \u203a Snap \u203a Planar \u00b7 Surfacing \u203a Stamp \u203a Planar"]},{"g":"n","t":"A new colour picker, built with KUI","b":"Every colour field now opens one colour picker, drawn with KUI, Klay's new shader-based interface. The compact card grows into a side panel with Values (HSV, RGB, HSL or OKLCH) and Swatches, plus a row of recent colours. For clay and poly paint the same card adds Channels, Variation and Mix tabs, replacing the tall paint colour panel. The card can be pinned open and closes with its cross.","w":["Any colour field"]},{"g":"i","t":"Brushes carry their custom alpha","b":"A brush saved or exported with a custom alpha now includes the alpha in its .klaybrush file, so a brush sent to someone else arrives with its stamp; on import the alpha is added to the stamp library. Brushes from earlier versions, which only point to a file in the library, load as before.","w":["Brush \u203a Save / Export"]},{"g":"i","t":"Pen pressure ranges and an Operator section for Stamp brushes","b":"A Stamp brush's Pen pressure card now sets a range from a light touch to a full press for Strength, Size, Plane offset and Depth, like a poly brush. Invert swaps the two ends, so a hard press can cut below the plane instead of rising above it. Add / Carve, Planar, Elastique, Blend and Combine are now grouped in one Operator section, each with its own switch.","w":["Brush \u203a Pen pressure"]},{"g":"i","t":"Theatre menu edit: Essentials tab and clearer Boolean functions","b":"In the Theatre menu's edit list, the function picker has three tabs: A\u2013Z, Categories, which now shows one category at a time, and a new Essentials tab, a short list of the main clay and poly functions grouped by task. The picker now offers Boolean union, Boolean subtract, Boolean intersect and Boolean menu, each working on clay and poly selections alike. Boolean union does the same as the D key. They replace Boolean (clay), Boolean and Boolean (poly); buttons that already hold those keep working. The function that adds an empty clay layer is now called New clay layer, and its button reads +Clay.","w":["Theatre menu \u203a Edit \u203a Functions"]},{"g":"i","t":"Sound levels for the interface and the ambience","b":"The Stroke Sound options now have level sliders for Monitor, UI and Ambience. UI sets the volume of the KUI interface sounds on the monitor; the other panels make no sound. Ambience replaces the old on / off switch for rain and thunder; at 0 it is off.","w":["Top bar \u203a Stroke Sound \u203a Level"]},{"g":"i","t":"Search in Settings","b":"A search field at the top of the Settings tab finds a setting by its card, sub-section, option or help text. Only the matching cards stay visible, and they open on the match. Press Esc or click the cross to clear it.","w":["Settings \u203a Search settings"]},{"g":"i","t":"Zen toolbar drawn with KUI","b":"The zen (icon-only) bottom toolbar and its brush pastille are now drawn with KUI, Klay's new shader-based interface. They keep the same buttons and layout.","w":["Bottom toolbar \u203a Zen"]},{"g":"i","t":"A faster, smoother brush wheel","b":"The wheel that opens while a shortcut number is held now opens and responds faster. Its cadrans open in a short sweep, and the hovered cadran grows slightly with its icon lifting. Picking a brush closes the wheel at once. The wheel is now drawn with KUI, Klay's new shader-based interface.","w":["Hold 1 to 0"]},{"g":"i","t":"Lighting presets keep Raytrace settings and can include the material","b":"Lighting presets now save the Raytrace settings that change the picture: bounces, max samples, Light & image (including Secondary bounces), Material offsets, Effects and the denoise strength. When the scene has a single material, saving a lighting preset asks whether to include it. A preset that carries a material shows the Material icon on its thumbnail, and loading it asks for Lighting only or With material.","w":["Lighting \u203a Presets \u203a Save to vault"]},{"g":"i","t":"Any floor height","b":"The Floor height slider of the Image and Procedural environments now covers -10 to 10, and any other value can be typed.","w":["Lighting \u203a Environment \u203a Floor height"]},{"g":"i","t":"Drag the lights in the Lantern like hold-S","b":"In the Lantern tool, a drag on empty space now rotates and lifts the lights like the hold-S drag, and the cursor shows the same bulb. With a light selected, that light turns alone. A click on empty space still deselects it.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Tools \u203a Lantern"]},{"g":"i","t":"View one channel across the scene","b":"The Paint tab's view strip shows Color, Roughness, Metalness, Normal or Alpha for every material in the scene, including texture maps, vertex colour and paint. Normal includes the normal map.","w":["Paint \u203a View strip"]},{"g":"i","t":"A clearer Paint tab header","b":"The top of the Paint tab now has two rows: the channel view strip, then Add layer with Group, Export, Channel matrix and Delete. The layer count moved to the bottom of the tab. The Material base card at the bottom of the stack expands into the full material settings, the same card as in the Material tab, and the baked maps have their own row under it.","w":["Paint"]},{"g":"i","t":"Color on the Polygone toolbar","b":"The Color tile is now on the Polygone toolbar as well and sets the brush's vertex paint. The compact palette also lists Albedo, SPR, Metal and, on clay, Emission, each with a toggle and a slider.","w":["Toolbar \u203a Color"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smooth also softens paint","b":"Brushes with Smooth can soften vertex colour and clay paint along with the shape. One undo restores both.","w":["Brush \u203a Paint channels \u203a Smooth color"]},{"g":"i","t":"A narrower function rail with names","b":"With its names shown, the function rail now places each name under a larger icon, so the rail is about 64 pixels wide instead of 156. In Edit mode, the Names switch returns the names beside the icons. When the rail is taller than the window, a thin scroll bar appears on its edge.","w":["Function rail \u203a Edit \u203a Names"]},{"g":"i","t":"Separate layers keep each object whole","b":"Import as separate layers now makes one layer per object of the file, so a ZBrush subtool made of several pieces arrives as one layer. The new Also split loose parts toggle gives each piece its own layer, as before.","w":["Import model \u203a Also split loose parts"]},{"g":"i","t":"Smoother Elastique strokes","b":"Stamp and Clay brushes with Elastique now stretch the clay in steps ten times finer, so a stroke at high Elastique no longer advances in visible jumps. The new Update warp slider sets the step for each brush; lower values are smoother and use more GPU time.","w":["Brush \u203a Elastique \u203a Update warp"]},{"g":"i","t":"Clay stamps lie on the surface","b":"On clay (SDF) layers, with Surface snap on, a shaped stamp such as a disk or a diamond now turns to the surface under the cursor, with or without Path follow. The rotation set with R is kept relative to the surface. The new Update normal slider sets how fast the stamp follows the surface: lower values stop it flickering on noisy surfaces. Path follow is now in Placement \u203a Snap and works with primitive and custom clay stamps. A stroke that runs off the edge of a model keeps the stamp's last orientation.","w":["Brush \u203a Placement \u203a Snap \u203a Update normal \u00b7 Path follow"]},{"g":"i","t":"Plane settings in the Operator Blend","b":"On poly brushes, the plane settings for Plane push and Flatten are now in a Planar card at the bottom of the Operator Blend, with Plane sampling inside it. They were in Stamp & Falloff \u203a Advanced stroke.","w":["Brush \u203a Operator Blend \u203a Planar"]},{"g":"f","t":"Copies of a mesh whose subdivision level is stored as tiles now appear in the viewport, cast shadows and render, including the copies made by the Modifier tab (Grid, Radial, Array). Copies show at a lighter display density than the original."},{"g":"f","t":"Mirrored copies (the Mirror modifier and Instance X) of an object scaled differently on each axis no longer shade dark in PBR and PBR Fast. A new Mirror modifier now reflects across the world axes by default."},{"g":"f","t":"The preview of a clay brush or stamp under the cursor is now drawn with PBR Fast shading instead of full PBR, whatever the layer's material, so it costs less to draw."},{"g":"f","t":"Mirror in Spatial mode no longer leaves the replaced half's vertices behind as ghost vertices, so a Cleanup pass is no longer needed afterwards. Undo still restores the mesh as it was."},{"g":"f","t":"Part of a mesh deleted with the Laser no longer comes back when you Subdivide. This mostly affected meshes made with Voxelize."},{"g":"f","t":"Fast strokes on poly meshes no longer break into straight segments. Pen strokes follow a smooth curve between tablet samples, and the stroke keeps the same shape with Cap FPS to display refresh on or off."},{"g":"f","t":"A lighting preset saved or loaded while the Lantern tool was active no longer moves the key light around the scene, and a pinned key light stays pinned."},{"g":"f","t":"Import as separate layers now keeps the file's UVs when Import UVs is on. Each layer used to arrive without them."},{"g":"f","t":"Klay motion recordings no longer include deleted or hidden objects. The OBJ sequence and the Klay cache now contain only the objects listed in the outliner and visible when each frame was captured."},{"g":"f","t":"Klay geometry cache files (.klaycache) now appear in the Import file browser and load as a recording on the timeline. A recording selected in the outliner is now highlighted like any other object."},{"g":"f","t":"Opening the Flood tab on a very dense mesh no longer freezes or closes the app. Its preview uses much less GPU memory, and a stack that does not fit now shows a message instead."},{"g":"f","t":"Flood stacks, such as Displace texture, no longer open cracks along the UV seams of a mesh imported with UVs, whether applied to the mesh or to a new layer. Apply to > New Flood layer now creates the Flood layer; it used to apply to the mesh."},{"g":"f","t":"Applying a material from the presets or the vault no longer crashes the app when contact shadows are on. Settings saved with out-of-range ambient occlusion values are repaired at launch."},{"g":"f","t":"Holding S to rotate the lights now works on empty space when Settings > Navigation > Void is on. The press used to orbit the camera instead."},{"g":"f","t":"Holding a shortcut assigned to a promoted section, such as Tessellation, and clicking in the viewport no longer crashes the app. Sections are no longer offered as shortcut targets."},{"g":"f","t":"Brush tessellation on meshes under about one million vertices no longer pauses at the start of every stroke."},{"g":"f","t":"Orbiting close to a dense subdivided mesh with level of detail on is smooth again. A view that level of detail could only draw coarsely now shows the full mesh, so the surface no longer shimmers while you turn around it."},{"g":"f","t":"Video memory no longer keeps rising during long Grab and Move sessions on very dense meshes. The undo history now stays in system memory."},{"g":"f","t":"Vertex colour, with its painted roughness and metalness, is now kept through Subdivide and when moving between subdivision levels. Detail painted on a higher level is kept when returning to it."},{"g":"f","t":"The burning save-reminder cursor now goes out as soon as Save, Save As or Version up is clicked. It used to stay lit while the file was written, and sometimes kept burning after the save."},{"g":"f","t":"Each stamp brush now keeps its own primitive and its settings. Switching between stamp brushes used to give all of them the last primitive used."},{"g":"f","t":"A disk, diamond or other shaped stamp now keeps its shape with Elastique Stretch at any value. It used to turn into a sphere."},{"g":"f","t":"The eye on a scatter set's target line in the outliner now turns that target on or off. It used to switch the first target only."}],"history":[{"version":"0.0.61","date":"2026-11-16","lede":"Clay Grab fixes: no debris after long Move and Elastique pulls, an exact Ctrl scale preview, and no flicker on release","highlights":["In the Primitives tool, a right-click on any primitive selects it and opens Swap shape, with its shapes and Blending","The Windows installer now updates Klay in the folder it was installed in, instead of proposing the default Program Files folder each time","Pen pressure works again on Linux, macOS and Windows Ink tablets","A long Move or Elastique pull on clay no longer leaves brick-shaped pieces floating along the pull after release","Scaling (Ctrl + drag) and twisting (Ctrl + right-drag) clay with the Grab tool no longer show the moved area cut flat in blocky steps while the button is held","A clay layer no longer disappears for one frame just after releasing some large grabs"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.61","items":[{"g":"f","t":"In the Primitives tool, a right-click on any primitive selects it and opens Swap shape, with its shapes and Blending. A right-click on a primitive that was not selected used to open the scene menu instead."},{"g":"f","t":"The Windows installer now updates Klay in the folder it was installed in, instead of proposing the default Program Files folder each time."},{"g":"f","t":"Pen pressure works again on Linux, macOS and Windows Ink tablets. Since 0.0.60 most brushes ignored pressure there; Wintab tablets on Windows were not affected."},{"g":"f","t":"A long Move or Elastique pull on clay no longer leaves brick-shaped pieces floating along the pull after release."},{"g":"f","t":"Scaling (Ctrl + drag) and twisting (Ctrl + right-drag) clay with the Grab tool no longer show the moved area cut flat in blocky steps while the button is held. The preview now matches the result on release."},{"g":"f","t":"A clay layer no longer disappears for one frame just after releasing some large grabs."}]},{"version":"0.0.60","date":"2026-11-16","lede":"Klay Live across the internet, saving in the background without freezing, Klay and ZBrush navigation styles, faster and smoother clay sculpting, scenes with many more clay layers, a procedural studio backdrop for the environment, and SSS trace sets","highlights":["Klay Live across the internet","Navigation styles on the welcome screen","Lights can follow the camera","Procedural studio backdrop","Paint channels in the Brush tab","SSS trace sets"],"notesUrl":"https://klaysculpt.com/releases/0.0.60","items":[{"g":"n","t":"Klay Live across the internet","b":"Klay Live lets several people sculpt together in one scene: Go Live shares the scene with an invite code, and Join enters a session with that code. Joining now works when the routers on both sides block incoming connections, which is common on home networks. Klay connects the computers directly over UDP; the session stays encrypted and nothing passes through a server. On macOS, Klay asks for Local Network access and says so if it is denied.","w":["Share \u203a Go Live / Join"]},{"g":"n","t":"Navigation styles on the welcome screen","b":"The welcome screen has a new Navigation page that sets how the view is turned, moved and zoomed: Klay (Turntable, Arcball or Trackball) or ZBrush (Classic or Right-click), each with its own saved settings, a factory reset and a Try it viewport that runs the style on a clay sphere. The ZBrush style rotates with a drag on the background, moves with Alt, zooms when Alt is released during the drag, snaps or rolls the view with Shift and paints the mask with Ctrl; each of these gestures is also an option in Settings \u203a Navigation & binding. A Wiki entry on the welcome screen opens klaysculpt.com/wiki in the browser.","w":["Welcome screen \u203a Navigation"]},{"g":"n","t":"Lights can follow the camera","b":"Each light has a new Follow section. Turn it on and the light keeps its position relative to the camera as you orbit, turning around the model with the view; Height also follows the camera up and down, as an orbit or a straight lift. Delay sets how long the light takes to catch up, from instant to three seconds.","w":["Lantern \u203a Light \u203a Follow"]},{"g":"n","t":"Procedural studio backdrop","b":"The environment can now be a procedural studio backdrop instead of an HDRI: a uniform colour, a gradient or a glow, with a floor that catches shadows, up to four texture layers over a base colour, and ten presets alongside your own. React to light turns the backdrop into a lit dome with roughness, specular and metalness, shaded by the scene lights and their shadows; Flatten and Dome rotation press one side of the dome into a flatter wall without changing its size, and the texture layers can cover the floor, the wall or both. Right-click a preset to apply, overwrite, duplicate, rename or delete it, or to restore the factory presets. A preset you save now stores every backdrop setting, including React to light, the floor and its layers. Switching the source to Procedural turns off the grid floor disk, since the backdrop has its own floor. A preset can also store the scene lights, shown by a light badge on its tile; applying it then replaces the current lights or adds to them. The background, lighting, reflections and Raytrace all use the backdrop, and it is saved with lighting presets and scenes.","w":["Lighting \u203a Environment \u203a Source \u203a Procedural"]},{"g":"n","t":"Paint channels in the Brush tab","b":"Clay stamp brushes and Poly brushes have a new Paint channels section that sets what a stroke paints: albedo, SPR and metal, and emission on clay. Each channel has its own switch, and a channel that is off leaves the paint underneath unchanged. Albedo can be a colour, chosen with the usual colour picker, or Shade, which makes the existing colour lighter or darker by a percentage; Keep hue changes only its lightness. Imperfection varies every painted value slightly from one dab to the next, more with harder pen pressure when Follows pressure is on. Paint is deposited only while Channel sculpting is on in the side rail. Every brush now starts with albedo off and SPR on at 0.5. On Poly brushes, Strength (formerly Flow in Paint & Mask) is now in this section.","w":["Brush \u203a Paint channels"]},{"g":"n","t":"SSS trace sets","b":"Materials placed in the same trace set share subsurface light where their meshes touch or overlap, so a head and its ears or lips glow as one piece instead of showing a dark seam. The Trace set card creates, renames and deletes sets and assigns the material to one; a material outside any set scatters on its own, as before.","w":["Material \u203a Subsurface (SSS) \u203a Trace set"],"n":"Raytrace only"},{"g":"n","t":"New brushes stand out","b":"A brush marked Set as new shows its toolbar icon white-hot, like fired clay. Picking it shows a short notice; Got it, I saw it returns the icon to its usual colour. Set as new is in the brush's Accessibility section.","w":["Brush \u203a Accessibility \u203a Set as new"]},{"g":"n","t":"Export the undo history as a stop motion","b":"The quick undo strip has a film button that records the undo history as a Stop Motion recording. It opens the Export Undo History dialog, where you choose the range of steps, the file name and the folder. The recording opens as a layer with its own timeline track, and Klay returns to the step you were on. Steps that do not change the model, such as a selection, add no frame. The recording plays back on the timeline and can be exported per frame with Export Stop Motion.","w":["Quick undo strip \u203a Export the history as a stop motion"]},{"g":"n","t":"Klay wiki","b":"The Klay wiki at klaysculpt.com/wiki is published as a first draft. It has a page for every toolbar tool, every function and every sidebar tab, including Material, Lighting, Camera, Render, Filter, Flood, Baker, Room and Klay Live. Each page shows the real panel with every control numbered and explained. Pages for Canvas will follow.","w":["klaysculpt.com \u203a Wiki"],"n":"First draft"},{"g":"i","t":"Ribbon brushes are fully editable in the Brush tab","b":"The ribbon of a Poly brush such as wet slab now shows its curves as graphs in the Brush tab: the cross-section, the blendshape target and the tip profile, each under its own switch. They edit like the falloff curve. The blendshape Driver and the tip noise Pattern are now menus, and the profile Noise controls have been added.","w":["Brush \u203a Stamp & Falloff \u203a Profile (ribbon)"]},{"g":"i","t":"Mud physics across the whole clay layer","b":"Brushes with Enable mud physics now simulate the mud anywhere on the clay layer instead of in a small box around the stroke, and stay fast with up to a million particles. Pen pressure sets how thick the stream of mud is. A stamp brush with mud physics pours its mud in the stamp's shape, size and orientation. With Paint color on, the mud takes the brush colour, both while it moves and once it becomes clay, and the clay it lands on keeps its own colour. Mud leaves the brush with the stroke's motion, so a flick throws it, and it collides with the clay, with visible mesh objects and with the Disk. All of the mud now turns into clay when it settles, and the finished mud no longer leaves small holes in the surface. While it moves, the mud is drawn as soft spheres in the layer's own material (Fast or PBR). Particle size is now an absolute size in the layer's voxels, the same at every brush size, and sets both the drawn spheres and the baked volume. Material is now a list of presets (Liquid mud, Mud, Thick clay, Sand, Lava / Wax, Honey, Slime, Snow, Wet plaster) that set the sliders below it, and a mud stroke can be undone.
